title: Characterization of Eosinophil Subtypes and Disease-Specific Biomarkers in Eosinophilic Myocarditis (The EMBASSY Study)
summary:
Eosinophilic myocarditis is a rare inflammation of the heart. It occurs in people with inflammatory diseases in which certain white blood cells, called eosinophils, play an important role. This heart inflammation can be serious and, in some cases, life-threatening. One major challenge is that, especially at the beginning, it is often difficult to predict how strongly the heart is affected and how the disease will develop over time. Because the condition is very rare, there is no standardized treatment yet.

Doctors can measure different blood markers and examine the heart using routine cardiac tests. However, these markers often only show general signs of heart weakness or heart damage. They do not always reliably show whether there is active inflammation in the heart, how severe it is, or how the disease is likely to progress. This makes it difficult to choose the right treatment early on — for example, to identify who needs stronger treatment quickly and who is more likely to have a milder disease course.

With this study, we aim to address this gap. We will investigate whether certain blood markers that we identified in an earlier analysis can truly help predict the course of the disease. In addition, we will search for new blood markers that are specific to this condition and may help explain why the disease is more severe in some people than in others. We will also examine whether certain subgroups of eosinophils can help tailor treatment more precisely to each individual patient. For this purpose, we will also study, among other things, the genetic material of these cells.

Our goal is to predict as accurately as possible, already at the time of first diagnosis, how the disease is likely to develop. This could allow treatment to be adapted early and specifically to each person’s individual risk — for example, by using anti-inflammatory medication and appropriate treatment to support heart function.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
i. Common inclusion criteria (all groups)
1. Capacity to provide informed consent and written informed consent following medical information
2. Treatment and diagnostic evaluation at LMU University Hospital Munich or at the cooperating centers
3. Availability of the required biomaterials/samples (whole blood) within the defined time window

ii. Group-specific inclusion criteria (index group)
1. Initial diagnosis or relapse of active eosinophilic myocarditis of inflammatory rheumatic origin after the date of the favorable ethics committee opinion
a. Diagnosis according to the 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines on myocarditis, based on clinical, laboratory, imaging, and/or histopathological criteria
b. Included underlying inflammatory rheumatic diseases:
- Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA, formerly Churg–Strauss syndrome)
- Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome (i-HES)
2. Causal relationship between “myocarditis” and the “underlying inflammatory rheumatic/eosinophilic disease,” with other sufficient explanations excluded according to specialist assessment
3. Absolute peripheral eosinophil count within the normal range (0.05–0.5 G/L) or elevated (>0.5 G/L), according to laboratory-specific reference ranges

iii. Group-specific inclusion criteria (control groups)
1. Diagnosis of EGPA/HES without cardiac involvement, eosinophilic asthma, heart failure of non-inflammatory origin, or healthy status
2. Absolute peripheral eosinophil count within the normal range (0.05–0.5 G/L) or elevated (>0.5 G/L)
Exclusion criteria:
i. Common exclusion criteria (all groups)
1. Age <18 years
2. Lack of capacity to provide informed consent or lack of written informed consent
3. No measurable eosinophils in peripheral blood (“eosinopenia”)
4. Lack of availability of the required biomaterials/samples (whole blood) within the defined time window
5. Severe anemia of any cause (hemoglobin <7 g/dL)
6. Underlying malignant disease not in remission at the time of presentation

ii. Group-specific exclusion criteria (index group)
1. No evidence of an inflammatory rheumatic etiology of EM
   a. Acute infections, neoplastic/myeloproliferative diseases (e.g., myeloproliferative or lymphocytic HES variants, chronic eosinophilic leukemias, myeloproliferative neoplasms, myelodysplastic syndromes)
2. Myocarditis without evidence of tissue or peripheral eosinophilia
3. Eosinophilia without fulfillment of the ESC criteria for acute myocarditis
4. No causal relationship between “myocarditis” and “eosinophilic disease”
5. Complete remission of EM

iii. Group-specific exclusion criteria (control groups)
1. Eosinophilic cardiac involvement
